title: Like the Sky
description: Twenty minutes of open awareness. The mind as the sky, thoughts as passing weather. Few words.

segments.say: Sit comfortably, and close your eyes, or leave them half open, resting downward.
Take a few deep breaths, and let them out slowly.
Let your attention rest on the breath, so the mind can settle.
In the Tibetan traditions, the mind is compared to the sky.
Clouds, storms, sunshine. Everything passes through the sky. And the sky is not stained by any of it.
Thoughts and emotions are the weather. You do not have to be the weather. You can be the sky.
Now let go of the breath as an anchor.
Let your attention open. Sounds, sensations, thoughts. Everything can be here.
Do not choose anything. Do not push anything away.
When a thought appears, let it pass like a cloud. You do not need to follow it.
If you get lost inside a thought, that is fine. Noticing it is already coming back to the sky.
Notice the space where all of this happens. It has no edge.
Nothing to do. Nothing to reach.
If a strong emotion comes, it is weather too. Let it rain.
Now, slowly, feel the body sitting here again.
The sky is still there, even when you get busy. You can come back to it at any moment of the day.
When you are ready, open your eyes.
